dedupe_keys.name: wind fragility model for urban street trees tongji university

description: This open-access study develops a wind fragility model for urban street trees from a mechanical analysis of tree failure. The uncertainty of the key parameters was quantified for the species of interest, a vine copula was used for the joint probability distribution of tree geometric parameters, and the resulting fragility curves were validated against historical measured data. The authors motivate the work by the direct losses and indirect effects of falling street trees on structures, lifeline facilities and traffic, and suggest the model can identify high-risk streets and regions. Coverage: street tree species studied by the Shanghai team. Access: the article in Disaster Prevention and Resilience (2022, volume 1, article 7) is open access; no code or curve tables were found as a separate download. Licence: open-access article; no software licence. Caveats: species-specific parameters and validation data are local, so curves need recalibration elsewhere. Simulation uses: probability of street-tree failure in typhoons, and tree-fall as a cause of road blockage and power line outages in cascading-failure models. Related records: the pre- and post-storm urban forest data protocol and the Noord-Brabant wind damage study.
